verdict: Goldman Sachs rode a dealmaking and trading boom to $20.3B of revenue (+39%) and $6.6B of profit (+78%) — equities revenue alone jumped 72% as markets stayed busy.

segments.name: Noninterest revenues
segments.note: Fees and trading: investment banking fees of $3.4B, FICC revenue of $4.6B and equities revenue of $7.4B, plus asset management fees.

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and investments, minus interest paid — a smaller, steadier slice for Goldman than for retail banks.

flow.costPlain: Money set aside for loans expected to go bad, mostly impairments on wholesale loans this quarter.

opex.name: Compensation and benefits
opex.note: Pay and bonuses — Goldman's biggest cost by far, rising with the firm's strong results.

opex.name: Transaction based
opex.note: Costs that rise and fall with trading and deal volume: brokerage, clearing and exchange fees.

opex.name: Communications and technology
opex.note: Trading systems, market data and communications.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of offices, systems and equipment over their useful lives.

opex.name: Occupancy
opex.note: Rent and running costs for offices around the world.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Everything else that does not fit the lines above.

takeaways.title: The boom was in banking & markets
takeaways.text: Global Banking & Markets revenue rose 53% to $15.5B: investment banking fees +55%, equities +72% and FICC +32% as IPOs, deals and trading all fired at once.

takeaways.title: Earnings per share nearly doubled
takeaways.text: EPS rose 92% to $20.98 and annualized return on equity was 23.5%. Profit grew much faster than revenue because the credit-loss provision fell to just $102M.

takeaways.title: Dividend raised
takeaways.text: Goldman raised its quarterly dividend to $5.00 per share (from $4.50) and returned $5.4B to shareholders in the quarter — $4.0B of buybacks plus $1.4B of dividends.

oneTimers: Platform Solutions revenue fell 64% to $221M, mostly on markdowns of the Apple Card loan portfolio (moved to held-for-sale in late 2025) — the last drag from Goldman's abandoned consumer push.
Preferred stock dividends of $229M sit between net earnings ($6,628M) and the $6,399M attributable to common shareholders.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
